title: Grateful Dead Live at Green Lake Aqua Theater on 1969-08-21
lineage: SBD > MC > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of a mellow 1969 Seattle show with standout Morning Dew and the debut Easy Wind, highlighted by Charles Lloyd’s (or Gary Larkey’s) flute.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑preserved soundboard tape that delivers clear, crisp audio with only a faint vintage hiss, preserving stage banter and ambient details. Musically the show is relaxed yet engaging, featuring a memorable early performance of “Easy Wind,” an emotive second half of “Morning Dew,” and a flowing sequence through “That’s It > The Other One > Dark Star > Cosmic Charlie.” The added flute adds a unique color without overwhelming the band.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is ~4.2/5 across 14 reviews; comments consistently praise both performance and sound quality, with only minor reservations.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with slight tape hiss; captures stage noises, bells, whistles, and vocal nuances. No major dropouts reported.

standout_songs: That’s It > The Other One > Dark Star > Cosmic Charlie
show_quality.setlist_flow: Relaxed, meandering vibe with smooth transitions; early Workingman's Dead classics open the set, followed by mellow mid‑song explorations and a cohesive second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Voice described as beautiful; noted playing pedal steel during New Riders opening and strong vocal presence on ‘Doin’ That Rag’.
band_member_comments.Keys: Flute addition (Charles Lloyd or Gary Larkey) works well, adding a unique texture.
band_member_comments.Drums: Smooth drumming; Kreutzmann and Hart’s mechanics highlighted as balanced and aged‑but‑good.
